import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify strongly associated features
    t_scores = [abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                   feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0]) 
                for fid in feats.ids]
    
    # Select top features by t-score
    top_indices = np.argsort(t_scores)[::-1][:20]
    top_ids = [feats.ids[i] for i in top_indices]
    
    # Find correlated pairs with |r| >= 0.6
    corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(top_ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(top_ids)):
            fid1, fid2 = top_ids[i], top_ids[j]
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(fid1)], 
                              feats.x[:, feats.column(fid2)])[0,1]) >= 0.6:
                corr_pairs.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # If we have correlated pairs, cluster them into modules
    if corr_pairs:
        all_features = set()
        for a, b in corr_pairs:
            all_features.add(a)
            all_features.add(b)
        
        # Use clustering to identify modules
        feature_list = list(all_features)
        n_features = len(feature_list)
        
        if n_features > 1:
            # Build correlation matrix
            corr_matrix = np.zeros((n_features, n_features))
            for i in range(n_features):
                for j in range(i+1, n_features):
                    r = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(feature_list[i])], 
                                  feats.x[:, feats.column(feature_list[j])])[0,1]
                    corr_matrix[i,j] = corr_matrix[j,i] = r
            
            # Cluster based on correlation
            clustering = AgglomerativeClustering(
                n_clusters=min(3, n_features), 
                linkage='average'
            ).fit(1 - np.abs(corr_matrix))  # Convert to distance
            
            # Get largest cluster
            labels, counts = np.unique(clustering.labels_, return_counts=True)
            if len(counts) > 0:
                main_cluster = labels[np.argmax(counts)]
                module_features = [feature_list[i] for i in range(n_features) 
                                 if clustering.labels_[i] == main_cluster]
                
                # Calculate weighted score using mean differences
                weights = {}
                for fid in module_features:
                    diff = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)]) - \
                           np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])
                    weights[fid] = diff
                
                # Normalize weights
                w_sum = sum(abs(w) for w in weights.values())
                if w_sum > 0:
                    for fid in weights:
                        weights[fid] /= w_sum
                
                # Return design with module features
                return Design(
                    drivers=tuple(module_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]),
                    columns=tuple(module_features),
                    products=(),
                    loadings=weights
                )
    
    # Fallback to simple approach
    if len(top_ids) > 0:
        # Use top 3 features as drivers
        drivers = tuple(top_ids[:MAX_DRIVERS])
        # Use all top features for regression
        columns = tuple(top_ids)
        # Simple weighting by t-scores
        weights = {}
        for i, fid in enumerate(top_ids):
            weights[fid] = t_scores[i]
        
        # Normalize
        w_sum = sum(weights.values())
        if w_sum > 0:
            for fid in weights:
                weights[fid] /= w_sum
        
        return Design(
            drivers=drivers,
            columns=columns,
            products=(),
            loadings=weights
        )
    
    # No mechanism found
    return Design(
        drivers=(),
        columns=(),
        products=(),
        loadings={}
    )
